doc.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Copenhagen recordings, interests and views on the music
title: They All Seem to Disappear and Jelly Brown
summary: McLean explains his childhood friend Walter Jelly Brown, who died strung out, and the kid material and pharaoh costume on the record.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: The other day, I was going through playing all this stuff, and I actually played one tune over and over again. It was They All Seem to Disappear. You mention this guy, Walter “Jelly” Brown. Was that a fictional character?

No, that was my man Jelly, Walter Brown. He was a real guy. He was my running buddy. We were kids together. We both started playing music together. I started on saxophone. He started on the clarinet. But he never continued to pursue it. Both got strung out. He eventually died in Texas somewhere, messing with some stuff.
But there was a sort of sentiment there that must be ever more with you.

Not – beyond, because the first part was about Jelly, and then you played some, and then it was about, or at least they patched in the playing, according to your recollection of it. But then you start talking about Bird and . . .

That was set up like that. They All Seem to Disappear. This guy that wrote the music on there, he had all that in his mind. But the thing that I loved the most on there is that very first track. It’s so nice. That’s my favorite recording – one of my favorite recordings, ever, because I like the instruments on there and everything. But all of that other stuff, Dr. Jackyll and Mister Funk and all of that stuff, that was some kid stuff. I took all my kids there from the program to be on it too. That’s another reason I did it, because he let me use – you can’t. There’s no centerpiece.
Oh yeah. I left those at home with the – that’s the one I said, well, there’s information on this record jacket – not the jacket, but the sleeve. But I had to protect.
Then I also wanted to be dressed up like a pharaoh. So they promised that to me too. So I said, oh man, that’s great.
